subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin thought Kalan was in the room with them the whole time.
source_quote: I thought Kalan was in the room with us this whole time,

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin decided to hand the confession to Kalan to let him save face.
source_quote: Alright," I said. "I think we just hand it to him — let him save face, since he got fired — with the understanding that they make good on the promise: we get our reward for helping crack the case."

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believed handing the case to Kalan was simple and clean.
source_quote: Simple. Clean. For once a faction problem had an answer I could say out loud without wanting to walk into a wall.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wanted to know whether they wanted to be famous or fly under the radar.
source_quote: Okay, the alternative: if we make a big deal about being the ones who cracked it, that plays into our fame. But do we really want to be famous, or do we want to fly under the radar? That's kind of our—

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin didn't know whether Dawnbringer was male or female.
source_quote: I don't know, I can't remember.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin accepted that Dawnbringer was female.
source_quote: Whatever — she. Yeah, I think we said she.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wanted to find a magic book to prove Bookwyrm's culpability.
source_quote: There's got to be a book somewhere in the library we can use to actually get to the bottom of this. Some sort of magic book. A powerful spell.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believed using the reward to get a book after the fact was better than acting upfront.
source_quote: So you wish to cast another spell on her?... I'm just thinking — the reversal here is: we go in, we say here are the people that did it, we get a reward, and one of us uses that reward to get the book that can then prove she did it.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz refused to rely on anything but the option of hacking and slashing if things went wrong.
source_quote: If things go sideways, we can always start hacking and slashing.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz found the hacking-and-slashing contingency comforting.
source_quote: It is not, strictly, a plan. It is comforting to him anyway.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believed being infamous underground hadn't served them well.
source_quote: We're already infamous underground. It didn't seem to serve us well.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed that Kalan had written the standard that now protected Bookwyrm.
source_quote: I filed that quietly under the column marked *irony*. The man wrote the standard, and the standard he wrote now shelters the person we most want to reach.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir questioned whether Kalan's plan was immoral by denying Bookwyrm a chance to serve if innocent.
source_quote: But from your own perspective — isn't that immoral? We're effectively preventing Bookwyrm, if innocent, from serving this role.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir wanted to know whether Kalan would give a full report if Bookwyrm declined the Zone of Truth.
source_quote: Okay — so you're willing to tell them everything we've learned if she declines?

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalled having done something similar for a mushroom.
source_quote: I know the arithmetic of that. I have done it for a mushroom.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum thought Kalan's patience strategy was clever but risky.
source_quote: *Sometimes the clever play is to be patient.* I thought, for half a breath, of a gold dragon who studied one chess position for four hundred years and lost it to a man who couldn't play.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recognized Kalan's plan as a familiar tactic from Gracklstugh.
source_quote: I have seen this move before, in Gracklstugh, dressed in different robes.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed Bookwyrm was covering for family.
source_quote: That part I believed. Whatever else Bookwyrm was, she was covering for family.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch refused to sneak or cast Zone of Truth without Bookwyrm's permission.
source_quote: I will not sneak this time. We will walk in, and we will boldly demand that she submit to a Zone of Truth.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch was afraid of making Bookwyrm his boss if he acted aggressively.
source_quote: He's not going to do it without her permission — how about I put it that way?

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch believed patience was the clever play.
source_quote: *Sometimes the clever play is to be patient.*

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch was pleased to have a research problem to solve.
source_quote: Kalan paused, and thought, and looked genuinely pleased to have a problem he could research.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch intended to find a book that could prove Bookwyrm's culpability after the naming ceremony.
source_quote: I will come up with such a book before you leave.

subject: Dawnbringer's identity
fact: Dawnbringer's gender is uncertain and unresolved.
source_quote: I don't know, I can't remember.

subject: Bookwyrm's guilt
fact: Bookwyrm's guilt remains unproven despite the suspicion.
source_quote: The confession is one spell — the weakest channel, by the standard I wrote. The heart and the cleaver prove someone covered this up cleverly. Neither says who it was.

subject: The magic book
fact: The specific magic book needed to prove Bookwyrm's culpability has not yet been identified.
source_quote: I don't know which book exactly, but I'm just thinking,

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is savoring the plan and building the stage in his head.
source_quote: I could hear him building the stage in his head.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes the plan is high drama and a good closing.
source_quote: High drama," Thorin said, and I could hear him building the stage in his head. "It'd be a good closing — she thought she got away with it, and then: one more thing.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wants to call out the fact that Bookwyrm is guilty.
source_quote: So, Thorin," I said, "this goes back to your strategy. Do we let on that we know more, or leave it till later, when we can really prove her involvement?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin thinks the red herring coin is funny and a sign of the safe's builder having nothing to hide.
source_quote: "Is there a red herring in there?" Thorin asked. There was, in fact. One of the gold coins had a herring stamped on it, and the herring was red. "That's funny," Daz said. It was the kind of joke that tells you the man who built the safe had a sense of humor and nothing to hide — which is its own kind of tell.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin approves of the grift and says "Never miss an opportunity to grift, man."
source_quote: "Never miss an opportunity to grift, man," Thorin said.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz refuses to drink the tea because he suspects Bookwyrm may have done something.
source_quote: Daz did not touch the cup in front of him. "I'll make it a little awkward — I'm certainly not drinking any tea from somebody we suspect may have done this."

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believes in withholding critical details to test if someone is deceiving or helping.
source_quote: I've been watching a lot of these 48-hour plays. What the guards always do is they withhold — they give enough information to say, we're on to it, we need your help. But they hold back the critical detail about the person being interviewed, so that if the person says something that doesn't match what the cops already know, they know they've got something more to investigate. My take: be a little shy with the full details, but give enough to make it look like they could tell a story — and then we see whether they're motivated to deceive us, or to actually help.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz notices that Bookwyrm is not sad but relieved.
source_quote: She was not sad. She was relieved.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realizes Bookwyrm is delighted to have the adventurers out of the way.
source_quote: Daz found the other half, the half I only saw land on his face: she was delighted to have us wrapped up and out of everything, no more heads poking anywhere.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is still weighing whether to cure Daral.
source_quote: "I mean, if he's… I don't know," Daz said, which is Daz for *I'm still weighing it, and it hasn't landed yet.*

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is waiting in Deneir's Sanctum and is watching the room carefully.
source_quote: I read the room the way I read every room. Books, a bored acolyte, four escapees who trust nothing. Worth watching. Worth remembering.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum remembers the Underdark lesson to spend cheap risk before dear risk.
source_quote: The Underdark teaches you to spend the cheap risk before the dear one, and I have never once regretted the lesson.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes theater is the work and does not correct Thorin's theatrics.
source_quote: I did not correct the theatrics. The name for the move was not wrong. And theater is the work; I of all people know that.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir knows the real crime is embarrassment, not murder.
source_quote: I only took notes and marked, in the margin, that we had come all this way to convict a woman not of murder but of embarrassment, and that everyone in the room seemed content with the trade.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes Bahamut may be reading over his shoulder.
source_quote: Bahamut may or may not have been reading over my shoulder. I wrote it down either way.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir tells Glabbagool to stay quiet during the tea moment as a moment of quiet reflection.
source_quote: I had told him first, low, that this was a moment of quiet reflection. No loud noises.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recognizes Glabbagool's restraint as discipline or the beginning of it.
source_quote: He stayed still because I asked him to. That is discipline, or the beginning of it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realizes Bookwyrm is not surprised but has already decided she has won.
source_quote: This was not that. The tears were correct and the eyes behind them were doing something else... She had decided.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir notices Bookwyrm's hands are too relaxed, indicating she has won.
source_quote: Her hands were too relaxed.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes Bookwyrm is sincerely afraid something will happen to them, but also delighted to have them out of the way.
source_quote: I looked at her while she said it and found, underneath, that she meant the worry. It was real — she was sincerely afraid something would happen to us. Daz found the other half, the half I only saw land on his face: she was delighted to have us wrapped up and out of everything, no more heads poking anywhere.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir steals the potion of flying with Glabbagool's arm and considers it a clean move.
source_quote: Glabbagool's arm came out low and quiet, the way I'd have wanted it if I'd trained him for it, which I had not, not yet. It closed around the vial, drew it back, and no one turned. Not one head. Everyone was frantically looking at everything else, and the thing nobody was looking at was me, and the ooze at my side, and the potion that had just left the box. Clean. Not lucky — clean.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir uses Locate Object to check if Bookwyrm has a sapphire, hoping she does.
source_quote: I wanted to know if she had one on her — that would have been interesting.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realizes Glabbagool liked the flying skill.
source_quote: Glabbagool was pleased with himself. *I like the flying skill,* he offered. *That was a good skill.*

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir plans to have a later conversation with Glabbagool about restraint.
source_quote: There would be a conversation later about restraint. Not now.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes Bookwyrm will never think to open the safe again.
source_quote: Everyone so fixed on their own troubles that they sealed a box they'd never think to open again and put Kalan Strongbranch back in charge of guarding it, full of himself and his methodology.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir lifts the tea cup and lets Glabbagool drink the tea instead of him.
source_quote: I lifted the cup, tilted it to my mouth, and let the tea run down into Glabbagool instead of down my throat.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir swipes the potion of flying off the table while everyone is distracted.
source_quote: While she was talking, I had my Glabbagool arm swipe the potion of flying off the table.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz goes quiet and still when he notices Bookwyrm is not sad but relieved.
source_quote: Daz caught it too — I saw him go quiet and still, the way he does when he's found the seam in a thing.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin asks if there is a red herring in the safe.
source_quote: "Is there a red herring in there?" Thorin asked.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir casts Locate Object to detect a sapphire on Bookwyrm.
source_quote: If any of us can Locate Object," I said. "Or Detect Object, whatever it's called. A sapphire. I wanted to know if she had one on her — that would have been interesting.

subject: Daral's cure
fact: Daral is afraid he will be left broken because the party may not consider him worth the spell.
source_quote: Are you guys going to cure me or anything?" he asked, and there it was — under the scholarship, the small fear of being left broken because we'd decided he wasn't worth the spell.

subject: Bookwyrm's sapphire
fact: Zalthir wanted to know if Bookwyrm had a sapphire, but none was found, leaving its significance unresolved.
source_quote: I wanted to know if she had one on her — that would have been interesting. The spell went out and found nothing. Bookwyrm did not have it.

subject: Bookwyrm's involvement
fact: The party knows Bookwyrm is guilty but lacks proof, leaving her fate unresolved.
source_quote: All we had was that she'd been in the same wing, and that Alkrist had named her the mastermind. Thin.

subject: Glabbagool's restraint
fact: Zalthir plans to discuss restraint with Glabbagool later, but the conversation has not yet occurred.
source_quote: There would be a conversation later about restraint. Not now.

subject: I
fact: I could have cast lesser restoration myself, but chose to hold my tongue and let others decide because I trusted the room would move toward mercy.
source_quote: I could have done it myself. Lesser restoration is cheap and I had it to spend — I can always cast another on people, if we don't want to die, and Daral wasn't going to die. But a man shouldn't sit in his own rot while four strangers debate his usefulness. So I held my tongue and let the room work it out, because it was working itself toward mercy, which is the only direction I ever need it to go.

subject: I
fact: I did not correct Zalthir when he suggested Daz might extort Daral, because I agreed with his assessment.
source_quote: I did not correct him. The read was not wrong.

subject: I
fact: I thought the interaction between Dawnbringer and Daral was a small good thing in a room full of guards.
source_quote: I thought, *there it is, a small good thing in a room full of guards.*

subject: I
fact: I believed the relationship between Dawnbringer and Daral was simple, rare, and truthful after the year I've had.
source_quote: These relationships are so complicated. This one, for once, was simple.

subject: I
fact: I understood that helmed horrors were chosen as assassins because they cannot talk, revealing the enemy’s intent to leave no one to interrogate.
source_quote: Of course. A killer with no mouth and no mind — whoever built these chose them precisely so there'd be nobody to squeeze afterward.

subject: I
fact: I remembered the giants' lesson that you don't chase, you position, and let the ground guide your actions.
source_quote: The giants taught me that before I could carry a shield — you don't chase, you position, and the ground under your feet says what your mouth doesn't need to.

subject: I
fact: I wanted to know who sent the helmed horrors and considered using a dead horror as a divining rod to detect who else had the key.
source_quote: Can we grab one of them and use it to detect who else has the key? Turn it into a sort of divining rod, as it were.

subject: I
fact: I noticed the helmed horrors were hovering a hand's width off the floor, which made my neck itch.
source_quote: Suits of plate with nobody inside, walking and — this was the part that made my neck itch — hovering, lifting a hand's width off the floor and drifting.

subject: I
fact: I realized the helmed horrors were not targeting people but following the key in Daz's pocket.
source_quote: They weren't following a face. They were following the key itself, sniffing it out through plate and pocket both.

subject: The key's origin
fact: The key’s origin and the identity of who sent the helmed horrors remain unknown.
source_quote: Somebody built these, aimed them, and put them through the windows knowing exactly which pocket to reach for.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes Daral should be let go and does not think extorting him would be nice.
source_quote: I don't think he had anything to do with it... I think we probably just let him… let him go." and "Yeah — we could extort him, but I don't think that would be nice.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin fondly acknowledges that Dawnbringer enjoys being called beautiful and worthy of study.
source_quote: Dawnbringer eats it up, I'm sure," Thorin said, fond.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir murmured that Daral would have bolted for the door if they had let him go.
source_quote: Zalthir murmured something about Daral bolting for the door the second we did.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir thinks Daz might extort Daral, but doubts the rest of the group would.
source_quote: Yeah — we could extort him," Thorin said, "but I don't think that would be nice." "I mean, maybe Daz would," Zalthir said. "But I don't know about the rest of us.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral intends to make the study of sentient swords his life’s research subject.
source_quote: I intend to make it an area of active research.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is confident he has enough healing spells and Revivify to cover Daz if he falls.
source_quote: Don't worry, I've got plenty of heal spells, buddy. If you get knocked out, I'll just heal you — you'll be back up in no time." A beat later: "I also have Revivify, so we're covered either way.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized the helmed horrors were not targeting him personally but were drawn to the key in his pocket.
source_quote: By then Daz had worked out what these things wanted, and it wasn't him — it was the key in his pocket.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the key in his pocket was inert under every spell they had cast.
source_quote: A key that read as nothing under every spell we'd thrown at it. Dead. Inert.
